answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit copper bond in the river registry and files one key-signed river record. A ridge auditor compares it against every record, charging 2 credits per comparison, plus a 15-credit fee. The k-th fake pays 75+2(k-1) credits: 60 locked, 15 fee, 2(k-1) audit fees, or 2073 for the 1000th. 1000 fakes total 1074000: 60000 bonds, 15000 fees, 999000 audit fees. An honest agent pays 75 once and recovers the 60 bond if unique. A rented-record ring reusing or tweaking one river record fails, since pairwise comparison flags near-duplicates and burns the bond.
